original_value: Image scene recognition is a core technology for many aerial remote sensing applications. Different landforms are inputted as different scenes in aerial imaging, and all landform information is regarded as valuable for aerial image scene recognition. However, the conventional features of the Bag-of-Words model are designed using local points or other related information and thus are unable to fully describe landform areas. This limitation cannot be ignored when the aim is to ensure accurate aerial scene recognition. A novel superpixel-based feature is proposed in this study to characterize aerial image scenes. Then, based on the proposed feature, a scene recognition method of the Bag-of-Words model for aerial imaging is designed. The proposed superpixel-based feature that utilizes landform information establishes top-task superpixel extraction of landforms to bottom-task expression of feature vectors. This characterization technique comprises the following steps: simple linear iterative clustering based superpixel segmentation, adaptive filter bank construction, Lie group-based feature quantification, and visual saliency model-based feature weighting. Experiments of image scene recognition are carried out using real image data captured by an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). The recognition accuracy of the proposed superpixel-based feature is 95.1%, which is higher than those of scene recognition algorithms based on other local features.

result.paraphrase: Image scene recognition is a key technology in many aerial remote sensing applications. In aerial imagery, different landforms are treated as distinct scenes, and all landform information is considered valuable for aerial image scene recognition. However, conventional Bag-of-Words features are built from local points or related information, so they cannot fully represent landform regions. This drawback is significant when accurate aerial scene recognition is required. In this study, a new superpixel-based feature is proposed to characterize aerial image scenes. Based on this feature, a Bag-of-Words scene recognition method for aerial imaging is then designed. The proposed feature uses landform information and links top-level superpixel extraction of landforms to bottom-level feature vector expression. This characterization method includes simple linear iterative clustering-based superpixel segmentation, adaptive filter bank construction, Lie group-based feature quantification, and visual saliency model-based feature weighting. Image scene recognition experiments are conducted using real image data collected by an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). The proposed superpixel-based feature achieves 95.1% recognition accuracy, outperforming scene recognition algorithms based on other local features.
